UC Berkeley - Survival Guide

Berkeley gives anyone -- from new visitor to beloved alumni -- the chance to see the world with new eyes, eat food from all over the world, travel to incredible places near and far, and enjoy the perks of living in the beautiful Bay. The first UC, Berkeley is world-renowned for its activism, research (with more than 72 Nobel prizes and 16 chemical elements discovered), entrepreneurial spirit, and unique Bay Area culture. Often featured in top rankings lists, UCB is one of the most selective public universities, currently ranked #1 in the world.

Set on the east shore of San Francisco Bay, Berkeley is an urban town bordering the cities of Alameda, Emeryville, and Oakland. Adjacent to San Francisco, Berkeley is part college-town, featuring yearly concert series at its famous Greek Theater, spirited football games, and great local restaurants. Students, faculty, researchers, visitors and more come from all over the world, representing more than 96 countries and all 50 states. With over 1100 student organizations and 35,000+ registered students, UC Berkeley enables so many opportunities for students' voices to be heard and new innovations to be created. In the 60s, the school became the birthplace of the Free Speech Movement, and recently students even helped create the first student district in the country -- named District 7!

DINING AT CAL

Popular student hangouts include the Durant Food Court, with favorites like Gypsy's Trattoria Italiana (pastas, homemade calzones, and more), Thai Basil, Ramen, and Pancho's Mexican food. Some favorite spots include The Sunny Side Cafe, Cafe Durant (a breakfast/lunch haven), Koja Kitchen (originally a Korean-Japanese food truck), Top Dog (Berkeley's famous hot dogs), Pasta Bene, and even Garaje -- just across the bridge in San Francisco.

Want to treat yourself? Gather a few friends and take a trip to Homeroom, known for their creamy mac n cheese.

Have a sweet tooth? Head on down to Oxford Street and sample the award-winning vegan cinnamon buns at Cinnaholic.

STUDYING AT CAL

Studying at Berkeley requires careful planning and scheduling, occasional trips to faculty office hours, and finding the perfect place to study for you. Generally, it's important to plan schedules ahead by 1.5 to 2 weeks. Go over syllabi, homework, and reading lists to have a good idea of what professors expect. Students at Cal spend a great amount of time on assigned reading, whether from actual course textbooks or Readers -- an accumulation of additional articles, info sheets, and photos necessary for each class.

When going over homework and reading, it's suggested that you write down any questions, comments, or concerns on a notepad or in margins, to ask professors or GSIs (Graduate Student Instructors) later. Some favored study spaces include the Cesar E. Chavez Student Learning Center (open 24/7), the University Library (Doe), Moffitt Library, Free Speech Movement Cafe, C.V. Starr East Asian Library, and Strada Cafe -- just off campus.

Pro Tip: take a day or two before classes to scope out your academic department's building or ask around for great secret study spaces!

TRAVEL

The incredible thing about the Bay Area is the ease in traversing multiple cities, bridges, and more with public transportation. Access to two bus systems, a famous subway line, and on-campus shuttles opens up many adventures.

The Class Pass: During class registration, every student is given a Class Pass -- a sticker received each semester which pays for boarding on any AC Transit (East Bay) bus, as well as other discounts on campus and in the city. AC Transit connects riders to destinations throughout the East Bay (Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville) and has a line to San Francisco.

BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) is a train line connecting the East Bay to San Francisco -- a fast way to traverse multiple cities. Muni (San Francisco Municipal Transit) connects riders to destinations throughout SF via bus and underground railway. Uber/Lyft is also very popular, along with Zipcar for occasional car rentals.

Parking in Berkeley long-term usually requires a permit and a semester-long fee (sometimes $500+). Students who go car-free can walk virtually anywhere on campus and navigate easily without paying for gas or parking.

CAMPUS SLANG

Cal: Nickname for UC Berkeley, the first UC.
Golden Bear: Unofficial nickname for all Cal-affiliated students, faculty, and sports teams.
Oski: UC Berkeley's official mascot since 1941.
GSI: Graduate Student Instructor -- Cal's version of a TA.
Class Pass: A sticker received each semester allowing free boarding on AC Transit buses and discounts on campus and in the city.
